title: World Capitals Quiz: Can You Get 10/10?
hook: Ten capital cities. The last three trip up almost everyone. Ready?

questions.q: What is the capital of Japan?
questions.explain: Tokyo is Japan's capital and its biggest city.

questions.q: What is the capital of Italy?
questions.explain: Rome has been Italy's capital since 1871.

questions.q: What is the capital of Canada?
questions.explain: Queen Victoria picked Ottawa as the capital in 1857.

questions.q: What is the capital of Australia?
questions.explain: Canberra was built as a compromise between Sydney and Melbourne.

questions.q: What is the capital of Brazil?
questions.explain: Brasília replaced Rio de Janeiro as the capital in 1960.

questions.q: What is the capital of Turkey?
questions.explain: Ankara has been Turkey's capital since 1923, not Istanbul.

questions.q: What is the capital of Morocco?
questions.explain: Rabat is the capital. Casablanca is just the biggest city.

questions.q: What is the capital of New Zealand?
questions.explain: Wellington is the world's southernmost national capital.

questions.q: What is the capital of Nigeria?
questions.explain: Abuja officially replaced Lagos as the capital in 1991.

questions.q: What is the capital of Kazakhstan?
questions.explain: Astana took over from Almaty as the capital in 1997.

outro: So, how many did you get? Ten out of ten? Drop your score below!
description: Ten world capitals, from easy to tricky. Can you name them all?

title: Animal Quiz: Only Animal Lovers Get 10/10
hook: Ten animal questions. Number ten surprises almost everyone. Let's go!

questions.q: How many legs does a spider have?
questions.explain: All spiders have eight legs. Insects have six.

questions.q: What is the fastest land animal?
questions.explain: Cheetahs can top 100 km/h in short sprints.

questions.q: What is the largest animal that has ever lived?
questions.explain: Blue whales can grow to about 30 meters long.

questions.q: Which of these mammals can truly fly?
questions.explain: Bats are the only mammals capable of true flight.

questions.q: Which of these mammals lays eggs?
questions.explain: Platypuses and echidnas are the only egg-laying mammals.

questions.q: How many hearts does an octopus have?
questions.explain: Two hearts pump blood to the gills, one to the body.

questions.q: Which living bird lays the biggest eggs?
questions.explain: An ostrich egg can weigh about 1.5 kg.
questions.note: Source: San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance

questions.q: What is a group of crows called?
questions.explain: It's a murder of crows. A parliament is owls.

questions.q: Which mammal has the longest pregnancy?
questions.explain: Elephants carry their babies for up to 22 months.
questions.note: Source: San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance

questions.q: What color is a polar bear's skin?
questions.explain: Under that white-looking fur, polar bear skin is black.
questions.note: Their fur is actually see-through. Source: Polar Bears International

outro: So, how many did you get? Ten out of ten? Tell me your score below!
description: Ten animal questions, from spiders to polar bears. How many can you get?

title: Human Body Quiz: Can You Get 10/10?
hook: Ten questions about your own body. Bet you miss the last one!

questions.q: How many bones are in the adult human body?
questions.explain: Most adults have 206 bones.

questions.q: How many chambers does the human heart have?
questions.explain: Two atria on top, two ventricles below.

questions.q: What is the largest organ of the human body?
questions.explain: Your skin is your body's largest organ.
questions.note: The liver is the largest internal organ. Source: Cleveland Clinic

questions.q: What is the longest bone in the body?
questions.explain: The femur, your thigh bone, is the longest.

questions.q: What is the hardest substance in the human body?
questions.explain: Tooth enamel is even harder than bone.

questions.q: How many teeth does a typical adult have?
questions.explain: That's 32, counting all four wisdom teeth.

questions.q: Where is the smallest bone in your body?
questions.explain: The stapes, in the middle ear, is about 3.5 mm long.

questions.q: Which blood type can go to almost anyone?
questions.explain: O negative is the universal red blood cell donor.
questions.note: For red cells. Source: American Red Cross

questions.q: About how many bones is a newborn baby born with?
questions.explain: Babies have about 270 bones. Many fuse as they grow.

questions.q: Which body part gets oxygen straight from the air?
questions.explain: The cornea has no blood vessels, so it absorbs oxygen from air.

outro: So, how many did you get? Ten out of ten? Drop your score below!
description: Ten questions about the human body, from bones to blood types.

title: Landmark Quiz: Which Country Is It In?
hook: Ten famous landmarks. Can you name the country for every one?

questions.q: Which country is the Eiffel Tower in?
questions.explain: The Eiffel Tower opened in Paris in 1889.
questions.note: Source: Société d'Exploitation de la Tour Eiffel

questions.q: Which country is the Colosseum in?
questions.explain: The Colosseum in Rome is nearly 2,000 years old.

questions.q: Which country is the Taj Mahal in?
questions.explain: The Taj Mahal stands in Agra, India.

questions.q: Which country is Machu Picchu in?
questions.explain: This Inca city sits high in Peru's Andes mountains.

questions.q: Which country is Christ the Redeemer in?
questions.explain: The statue looks over Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.

questions.q: Which country is Angkor Wat in?
questions.explain: Angkor Wat is the world's largest religious monument.

questions.q: Which country is the ancient city of Petra in?
questions.explain: Petra was carved straight into rock cliffs in Jordan.

questions.q: Which country is Chichén Itzá in?
questions.explain: This Maya city is on Mexico's Yucatán Peninsula.

questions.q: Which country is Neuschwanstein Castle in?
questions.explain: This fairy-tale castle is in Bavaria, Germany.

questions.q: Which country do the Easter Island statues belong to?
questions.explain: Easter Island belongs to Chile, over 3,500 km offshore.

outro: So, how many did you get? Ten out of ten? Tell me your score below!
description: Ten famous landmarks around the world. Can you name the country each one is in?
sources: Société d'Exploitation de la Tour Eiffel

title: Food Quiz: Where Did It Really Come From?
hook: Ten foods. Where did they really come from? Number ten fools everyone.

questions.q: Which country are tacos from?
questions.explain: Tacos come from Mexico.

questions.q: Which country is nigiri sushi from?
questions.explain: Nigiri sushi was born in Edo, now Tokyo, in the 1800s.

questions.q: Pizza Margherita comes from which Italian city?
questions.explain: Pizza Margherita was born in Naples.
questions.note: Named for Queen Margherita, per the 1889 story. Source: Britannica

questions.q: Kimchi is a famous dish from which country?
questions.explain: Kimchi is a fermented cabbage dish from Korea.

questions.q: Paella comes from which country?
questions.explain: Paella comes from Valencia, Spain.

questions.q: Tomatoes first came from which continent?
questions.explain: Wild tomatoes come from South America, not Italy.

questions.q: Potatoes were first farmed in what is now which country?
questions.explain: Potatoes were first farmed in the Andes, in today's Peru.
questions.note: Near Lake Titicaca, on the Peru-Bolivia border. Source: International Potato Center

questions.q: Coffee plants first came from which country?
questions.explain: Arabica coffee is native to the forests of Ethiopia.

questions.q: The croissant was inspired by a pastry from which country?
questions.explain: It grew out of the Austrian kipferl, brought to Paris.

questions.q: Fortune cookies became popular in which country?
questions.explain: Fortune cookies took off in the USA, not China.
questions.note: They likely trace back to Japanese crackers. Source: Smithsonian

outro: So, how many did you get? Ten out of ten? Drop your score below!
description: Ten foods and where they really come from, from tacos to fortune cookies.

title: Planet Earth Quiz: Can You Get 10/10?
hook: Ten questions about our planet. Most people miss number seven!

questions.q: How many continents are there?
questions.explain: Most of the world counts seven continents.
questions.note: Using the common seven-continent model. Source: National Geographic

questions.q: What is the largest ocean on Earth?
questions.explain: The Pacific covers about a third of Earth's surface.

questions.q: What is the tallest mountain above sea level?
questions.explain: Everest stands 8,849 meters tall.
questions.note: 2020 survey by Nepal and China. Source: Britannica

questions.q: What is the largest country by area?
questions.explain: Russia covers about 17 million square kilometers.

questions.q: What is the largest hot desert on Earth?
questions.explain: The Sahara is the largest hot desert. Antarctica is the largest overall.

questions.q: Where is the deepest point in the ocean?
questions.explain: Challenger Deep is nearly 11 km down.

questions.q: What gas makes up most of Earth's air?
questions.explain: Air is about 78% nitrogen and only 21% oxygen.

questions.q: What is the largest island in the world?
questions.explain: Greenland is the largest island, not counting Australia.
questions.note: Australia counts as a continent. Source: Britannica

questions.q: Which continent has the most countries?
questions.explain: Africa has 54 countries.
questions.note: UN member states. Source: United Nations

questions.q: What is the deepest lake in the world?
questions.explain: Lake Baikal in Russia is over 1,600 meters deep.

outro: So, how many did you get? Ten out of ten? Tell me your score below!
description: Ten questions about planet Earth, from oceans to the deepest lake.

title: Halloween Quiz: Can You Get 10/10?
hook: Happy Halloween! Ten spooky questions. Can you survive all ten?

questions.q: What date is Halloween?
questions.explain: Halloween is October 31, the night before All Saints' Day.

questions.q: Who wrote the novel Dracula?
questions.explain: Bram Stoker published Dracula in 1897.

questions.q: Who wrote Frankenstein?
questions.explain: Mary Shelley published Frankenstein in 1818.

questions.q: Which region is Count Dracula from?
questions.explain: Stoker set Dracula's castle in Transylvania, Romania.

questions.q: Day of the Dead is celebrated mainly in which country?
questions.explain: Día de los Muertos is held on November 1 and 2.

questions.q: What does the name Halloween come from?
questions.explain: It means the eve of All Hallows, or All Saints' Day.

questions.q: Halloween grew from which ancient Celtic festival?
questions.explain: Samhain marked the end of summer and harvest.

questions.q: Botanically, a pumpkin is a…?
questions.explain: Pumpkins grow from flowers and hold seeds, so they're fruits.

questions.q: Jack-o'-lanterns were first carved from what?
questions.explain: In Ireland and other Celtic lands, people carved turnips first.
questions.note: Pumpkins came later. Source: Smithsonian, Britannica

questions.q: Which famous magician died on Halloween in 1926?
questions.explain: Harry Houdini died on October 31, 1926.

outro: So, how many did you get? Ten out of ten? Drop your score below!
description: Ten spooky Halloween questions, from Dracula to jack-o'-lanterns.
